23-tensors-autograd.summary: Represent data as tensors and let automatic differentiation compute gradients through a model.
23-tensors-autograd.why: Tensors and computation graphs are the working language of modern deep-learning frameworks.
23-tensors-autograd.practice: Inspect tensor shapes, devices, and gradients in a small PyTorch model.

23-datasets-dataloaders.summary: Create repeatable input pipelines that batch, shuffle, and transform examples.
23-datasets-dataloaders.why: Reliable pipelines keep model training fast and prevent data leakage.
23-datasets-dataloaders.practice: Write a dataset and data loader for a labeled image folder.

23-training-loop.summary: Connect forward passes, losses, gradients, optimizer steps, and metric logging.
23-training-loop.why: The training loop reveals where learning succeeds or fails.
23-training-loop.practice: Write a training loop without a high-level trainer and plot the loss.

23-validation-loop.summary: Measure generalization on held-out data and save the strongest checkpoint.
23-validation-loop.why: Training loss alone cannot tell you whether a model will work on new data.
23-validation-loop.practice: Add validation, early stopping, and checkpoint restoration to a training run.

23-learning-rate-schedules.summary: Change the learning rate during training to balance fast progress and stable convergence.
23-learning-rate-schedules.why: A schedule can make the same optimizer converge more reliably.
23-learning-rate-schedules.practice: Compare constant, cosine, and step schedules on one model.

23-residual-connections.summary: Add shortcut paths that help information and gradients pass through deep networks.
23-residual-connections.why: Residual connections made much deeper models practical to optimize.
23-residual-connections.practice: Implement a residual block and compare it with a plain stack of layers.

23-recurrent-networks.summary: Process sequences with a hidden state shared across time steps.
23-recurrent-networks.why: Recurrent networks explain many sequence-modeling ideas that preceded transformers.
23-recurrent-networks.practice: Train a compact recurrent model on a short sequence task.

23-model-debugging.summary: Use tiny batches, baselines, gradient checks, and learning curves to locate failures.
23-model-debugging.why: Most model problems come from data and training mechanics before architecture.
23-model-debugging.practice: Force a model to overfit one batch, then diagnose a deliberately broken pipeline.

23-experiment-tracking.summary: Record code, data, hyperparameters, metrics, and artifacts for every run.
23-experiment-tracking.why: Comparable records turn trial and error into evidence.
23-experiment-tracking.practice: Track three controlled runs and write a short decision log.

25-image-classification.summary: Assign one or more labels to an image and inspect performance by class.
25-image-classification.why: Classification is the clearest complete workflow for learning visual representations.
25-image-classification.practice: Fine-tune a classifier and review its confusion matrix and hardest examples.

25-feature-maps.summary: Trace how spatial features and receptive fields change across a convolutional network.
25-feature-maps.why: Shape and receptive-field reasoning helps diagnose weak vision architectures.
25-feature-maps.practice: Visualize feature maps from early and late layers of a trained CNN.

25-resnets.summary: Use residual blocks to train deep image encoders.
25-resnets.why: ResNets remain a strong baseline and a foundation for transfer learning.
25-resnets.practice: Fine-tune a small ResNet and compare frozen versus unfrozen layers.

25-object-detection.summary: Locate and classify multiple objects with bounding boxes.
25-object-detection.why: Detection combines localization, classification, and confidence calibration.
25-object-detection.practice: Run a pretrained detector and inspect false positives, misses, and duplicate boxes.

25-iou-map.summary: Measure box overlap with IoU and summarize detector quality with mean average precision.
25-iou-map.why: Detection needs metrics that reward both correct classes and useful localization.
25-iou-map.practice: Compute IoU for sample boxes and compare precision-recall at two thresholds.

25-yolo.summary: Predict object locations and classes in a fast, single-stage detector.
25-yolo.why: YOLO is a practical entry point for real-time detection systems.
25-yolo.practice: Fine-tune a small detector and measure accuracy and latency together.

25-image-segmentation.summary: Predict a class for each pixel to separate objects and regions.
25-image-segmentation.why: Segmentation is essential when the shape and area of an object matter.
25-image-segmentation.practice: Train a small binary segmenter and inspect masks at object boundaries.

25-unet.summary: Combine an encoder with skip-connected decoding for precise pixel masks.
25-unet.why: U-Net is a practical, widely used segmentation architecture.
25-unet.practice: Implement one encoder-decoder skip connection and compare mask quality.

25-vision-transformers.summary: Treat image patches as tokens and learn global visual relationships with attention.
25-vision-transformers.why: Vision transformers connect modern image systems with transformer foundations.
25-vision-transformers.practice: Compare predictions from a pretrained CNN and vision transformer on shifted images.

25-opencv.summary: Load, transform, annotate, and export images and video frames with OpenCV.
25-opencv.why: Production vision work needs dependable image and video processing around the model.
25-opencv.practice: Build a preprocessing pipeline that resizes, converts color, and draws predictions.

25-vision-error-analysis.summary: Group failures by class, source, lighting, resolution, and other meaningful slices.
25-vision-error-analysis.why: Aggregate accuracy can hide systematic failures in a vision system.
25-vision-error-analysis.practice: Create an error gallery and choose one data or modeling change from the evidence.

37-language-modeling.summary: Model the probability of token sequences and use it to generate language.
37-language-modeling.why: Language modeling is the central objective behind general-purpose LLMs.
37-language-modeling.practice: Score and compare a few short token sequences with a small open model.

37-next-token-prediction.summary: Predict the next token from preceding context and repeat the process autoregressively.
37-next-token-prediction.why: This simple objective creates surprisingly broad language capabilities at scale.
37-next-token-prediction.practice: Inspect next-token probabilities as you change one word in a prompt.

37-llm-tokenization.summary: Split text into reusable subword units and understand token counts and boundaries.
37-llm-tokenization.why: Tokenization affects cost, context length, multilingual behavior, and model inputs.
37-llm-tokenization.practice: Compare token counts for code, prose, numbers, and two languages.

37-positional-encoding.summary: Add information about token order to an attention-based model.
37-positional-encoding.why: Attention alone does not know which token came first.
37-positional-encoding.practice: Plot sinusoidal encodings and compare nearby and distant positions.

37-self-attention.summary: Let each token combine information from other tokens in the same sequence.
37-self-attention.why: Self-attention is the main routing mechanism inside transformers.
37-self-attention.practice: Calculate a tiny query-key attention example by hand.

37-multi-head-attention.summary: Run several learned attention projections in parallel and combine their outputs.
37-multi-head-attention.why: Multiple heads let a layer represent different relationships at once.
37-multi-head-attention.practice: Trace tensor shapes through a multi-head attention layer.

37-transformer-blocks.summary: Combine attention, feed-forward layers, normalization, and residual connections.
37-transformer-blocks.why: Repeated transformer blocks form the backbone of modern LLMs.
37-transformer-blocks.practice: Diagram one decoder block and label every residual path and tensor shape.

37-pretraining.summary: Learn broad language patterns from large text collections before task-specific adaptation.
37-pretraining.why: Pretraining creates reusable representations and generation behavior.
37-pretraining.practice: Compare base-model and instruction-model responses to the same prompt.

37-context-windows.summary: Manage the finite token budget available for instructions, evidence, and output.
37-context-windows.why: Context design affects cost, latency, recall, and answer quality.
37-context-windows.practice: Budget tokens for a prompt, retrieved passages, and a structured response.

37-instruction-tuning.summary: Adapt a pretrained model to follow human-written tasks and response formats.
37-instruction-tuning.why: Instruction tuning turns a base language model into a more useful assistant.
37-instruction-tuning.practice: Write five diverse instruction-response examples for one narrow task.

37-lora.summary: Adapt a model by training small low-rank matrices instead of every parameter.
37-lora.why: LoRA makes focused adaptation possible with much less memory and compute.
37-lora.practice: Estimate trainable parameters for full fine-tuning versus a LoRA setup.

37-prompt-design.summary: State the task, context, constraints, examples, and output contract clearly.
37-prompt-design.why: A precise prompt makes behavior easier to test and maintain.
37-prompt-design.practice: Create a prompt suite with normal, ambiguous, and adversarial cases.

37-structured-output.summary: Constrain model responses to a schema that software can validate and use.
37-structured-output.why: Reliable applications need parseable results, not loosely formatted prose.
37-structured-output.practice: Define a JSON schema and test repair behavior on invalid output.

37-embeddings-search.summary: Encode text as vectors and retrieve passages by semantic similarity.
37-embeddings-search.why: Semantic retrieval brings relevant private or current knowledge into an application.
37-embeddings-search.practice: Embed a small document set and inspect the top results for five queries.

37-vector-databases.summary: Index embedding vectors with metadata for fast filtered similarity search.
37-vector-databases.why: A retrieval layer must scale while preserving source and access information.
37-vector-databases.practice: Index chunk embeddings with document IDs and metadata filters.

37-rag.summary: Retrieve relevant evidence and place it in context before generation.
37-rag.why: RAG can ground answers in selected sources without retraining the model.
37-rag.practice: Build a document question-answering pipeline that returns source citations.

37-llm-evaluation.summary: Measure task success with fixed datasets, rubrics, traces, and human review.
37-llm-evaluation.why: LLM behavior varies, so changes need repeatable evaluation before release.
37-llm-evaluation.practice: Create a 20-case evaluation set and compare two prompts blindly.

37-hallucinations.summary: Detect unsupported claims and design grounding, citation, and abstention behavior.
37-hallucinations.why: Confident fabrication is a central product risk for generative systems.
37-hallucinations.practice: Label unsupported claims in model answers and test an abstention rule.

37-quantization.summary: Store and compute model weights at lower precision to reduce memory and latency.
37-quantization.why: Quantization can make capable models practical on smaller hardware.
37-quantization.practice: Compare model size, speed, and output quality at two numerical precisions.

37-inference-serving.summary: Serve model requests with batching, caching, observability, and resource limits.
37-inference-serving.why: A useful LLM product must control latency, throughput, reliability, and cost.
37-inference-serving.practice: Design an inference API and measure time-to-first-token and total latency.
